reading.body:
Equinix DC1 is a 19,935 square foot facility in Ashburn, Virginia with no published power capacity figure. The operator states it runs on 2N power redundancy, N+2 cooling redundancy, and N+1 generator redundancy with 30+ hours of autonomous runtime at full load, which qualifies it to host workloads requiring high availability. This building is one facility within Equinix's 15-building Washington DC metro region, the largest peering point in North America and a gateway to Europe.

Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, but only 23 have published power capacity figures totaling 1,375 megawatts. DC1 does not publish its power capacity, so it does not appear in the state's ranked published capacity figures. Without a megawatt figure, the effective size of this facility relative to the state's infrastructure cannot be derived from available data.

The redundancy profile indicates this is a high-tier colocation asset suitable for mission-critical tenants, but the absence of published power capacity means its contribution to Virginia's AI infrastructure cannot be quantified from operator disclosures. To assess whether this facility matters to AI scaling, the power budget would need to be disclosed by Equinix.
